title: Minimum Age to Ride a Motorbike or Moped in Vietnam
meta_description: Check minimum riding ages in Vietnam, how mopeds and motorbikes are defined, licence conditions and questions families should ask before renting.
h1: Minimum Age to Ride a Motorbike or Moped in Vietnam
body_markdown:
Families with teenagers and young travellers soon ask the same question in Vietnam: may a 16-year-old rent a scooter, and from what age is a proper motorbike allowed? You will see very young riders on the streets, but the law sets clear age limits, and they depend on whether the vehicle counts as a moped or a motorbike. This guide explains the age rules in the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety, the difference between the two vehicle classes, the penalties under [Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm) and what all this means for families. For the paperwork side, see our topic page on [rental documents and contracts](/en/topics/documents-and-contracts/).

## Moped or motorbike: the distinction that matters

Vietnamese law distinguishes two kinds of powered two-wheeler. A moped ("xe gắn máy") is, under [Article 34(1)(g) of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf), a two- or three-wheeled vehicle with a design speed of no more than 50 km/h; with a combustion engine its capacity may not exceed 50 cm³, with an electric motor its power may not exceed 4 kW. Anything above that is a motorbike ("xe mô tô") under point (e).

That matters to renters because the typical rental scooter in Hanoi is a motorbike in the legal sense: an automatic scooter with 110 or 125 cm³ is well above the moped limit. Genuine 50 cm³ mopeds and low-powered electric scooters are the exception. Our comparison of [50cc and electric scooters](/en/guides/50cc-vs-electric/) explains the options, and our guide to [Honda's common rental models](/en/guides/honda-wave-vision-air-blade-lead/) gives their engine sizes.

## The age limits in the law

[Article 59(1) of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) sets two thresholds:

- **From 16** you may ride a moped.
- **From 18** you may obtain licence classes A1, A, B1 and B. Under [Article 57(1)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf), class A1 covers motorbikes up to 125 cm³ or 11 kW and class A anything larger.

Below 16, nobody may ride any powered two-wheeler. At 16 or 17, only a moped of up to 50 cm³ or 4 kW is allowed, never a motorbike.

## Electric scooters: power is what counts

For electric scooters the deciding figure is motor power, not engine size. An electric scooter of no more than 4 kW with a design speed of no more than 50 km/h is a moped under [Article 34(1)(g)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) and may be ridden from 16. Above that it is a motorbike, so the licence rules and the minimum age of 18 apply; up to 11 kW, class A1 is enough under [Article 57(1)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf). Both kinds are on Hanoi's roads and they can look alike, so ask to see the power rating on the registration certificate before a teenager rides off.

## A moped needs no licence, but the rules still apply

Moped riders do not need a licence: [Article 56(1)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) expressly exempts them. Under [Article 56(4)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf), however, they must know the traffic rules, be able to control the vehicle safely and meet the age and health requirements. A 16-year-old on a moped for the first time in Hanoi traffic will struggle to meet that standard, and the helmet rules apply to mopeds just as they do to motorbikes.

## What the penalties are

[Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm) sets graded penalties in Article 18:

- **Aged 14 or 15:** riding a motorbike, a moped or driving a car brings a warning under Article 18(1) ([Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm)).
- **Aged 16 or 17:** riding a motorbike of 50 cm³ or more, or with an electric motor of 4 kW or more, costs 400,000 to 600,000 VND under Article 18(4)(a) ([Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm)).
- **Without the right licence:** riding a motorbike of up to 125 cm³ without a valid licence costs 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 VND under Article 18(5)(a), and above 125 cm³ 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 VND under Article 18(7)(b) ([Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm)).

The consequences after a crash can be much heavier than any of these amounts. Our guide to [what to do after a motorbike accident](/en/guides/after-a-motorbike-accident/) explains the first steps if something goes wrong.

## Health counts as well as age

Age is not the only condition. [Article 59(2)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) requires everyone who drives or rides to be in a state of health suited to the vehicle, and [Article 56(4)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) refers moped riders to the same requirement. Whatever your age, do not ride when you are exhausted, on medication that slows your reactions, or barely alert after a long travel day in the heat with jet lag.

## What it means for families

For parents of children under 16 the answer is clear: they may not ride themselves, but they may ride as passengers. Under [Article 33(1)](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf), a child under 12 may be carried as a second passenger on a motorbike, and everyone on the bike needs a properly fitted helmet.

Teenagers of 16 or 17 can only ride a moped of up to 50 cm³ or a low-powered electric scooter. Ask the rental shop specifically about engine size or motor power and check the figure on the registration certificate. A friendly "no problem" from the shop does not change the legal limits.

From 18, a motorbike may be ridden only with a licence of the right class that is valid in Vietnam. Our guides to [foreign driving licences](/en/guides/foreign-driving-licence/) and [International Driving Permits](/en/guides/international-driving-permit-motorbike/) explain what that means for visitors.

## Tips for young riders

- **Practise before the city.** Even a moped takes practice; do your first laps on a quiet street or an empty square.
- **Avoid rush hour at first.** Hanoi's evening traffic overwhelms experienced riders from abroad too.
- **Wear the helmet properly.** Fasten the strap, keep the visor clean and choose the right size.
- **No passengers at first.** A passenger lengthens braking distances and makes the bike slower to respond.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is there a minimum age for passengers?** No minimum age applies to passengers, but the rules on how many people may ride and the helmet requirement in [Article 33](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf) do.

**May my 17-year-old ride if I ride right next to them?** No. The age limits apply whether or not an adult is nearby, and a motorbike above 50 cm³ stays off limits at 17.

## In short

From 16 a moped of up to 50 cm³ or 4 kW is allowed in Vietnam, from 18 a motorbike with a licence of the right class ([Article 59](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/55-vbhn-vpqh.pdf)). Typical 110 or 125 cm³ rental scooters are motorbikes. Riders under 18 on one face a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND under [Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-168-2024-nd-cp-quy-dinh-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-ve-trat-tu-atgt-duong-bo-119241231164556785.htm), and riding without a licence costs much more. Before the first ride, our [rental pickup checklist](/en/checklist/) helps you check the bike and its papers.
